All five items are done. Items 1–4 are built and their focused test runs pass. For item 5 the code would **drop** the named party, so per your instruction I did not pin it.

Nothing is committed and `ops/check.sh` was not run. Only `crates/ingest/src/partyname.rs` and `crates/ingest/src/project.rs` changed; `docs/operations.md` and the issue file are untouched. The temporary probe tests I used for items 1–5 have been removed.

**Focused runs** (gate flags and package set, output redirected to a file, `EXIT` read):
- First run, items 1–4: EXIT=0, 43 ingest lib tests passed (the partyname module and the 511 project tests).
- Item 5 probe with `--nocapture`: EXIT=0.
- Final run after cleanup, filters `partyname project:: text:: role_census idgate placeholder translated withheld`: EXIT=0. The ingest lib passed 217 tests, all other binaries were green, and there was no FAILED line.

The new tests passed on the first run. I did not run them against the old code first. They target names the residual plan records as `name` or `award_summary` today, and the item-1 test asserts that each translation reads as a name on its own.

**Item 1 — TED translation echo**
- **Change:** `project.rs:4515/4534` now records each name's language label, and the new `translation_echoes` (`project.rs:4631`) runs before the decider's rules.
- **Rule:** an unclassified name counts as the party's `Placeholder` only when all of these hold:
  - it carries the same section-number token (`partyname::form_section_tokens`, `partyname.rs:744`);
  - both names have language labels and the labels differ;
  - it passes `translation_shaped` (`partyname.rs:766`): 12 words or fewer, and no legal form. The legal-form check combines `company_token`, the Polish form, `crosswalk::legal_form_family`, and `mbH`/`e.V.`/`gGmbH`.
- **Scope:** only the publisher's own `Placeholder` names seed the sweep, and an `AwardSummary` translation still keeps the party.
- **Tests:**
  - `a_teds_translated_pointer_is_dropped_with_its_translations` (`project.rs:14443`) uses the 24-language list for VI.2 and a VI.3 variant. Both parties drop, the result reads `selec-w` with no winner, and the counts in `mentions_and_dropped` match.
  - `a_name_beside_a_translated_pointer_that_reads_as_a_party_keeps_it` (`:14479`) keeps eight near-miss cases: a GmbH, a name over 12 words, a different number, the same language, no label, no dotted number, no number on the name, and an AwardSummary.
  - `form_section_tokens_and_the_translation_shape` (`partyname.rs:2634`).
- **Doubt — reconstructed strings:** the PL, SK, SL, GA, BG, RO and HR strings in `TED_VI2_POINTER` are written from TED's labels because your read was truncated. The comment on the constant says so.
- **Doubt — language labels:** the rule depends on r208 copies carrying their `LG` label, which the r209 parser emits.
- **Doubt — the walk's net:** the net still only sees the org's head name. A notice whose original language is not English, so that the head name is a translation, is invisible to the walk, though a refold still drops it. The 460 residual orgs all have English head names.

**Item 2 — form section titles after a pointer**
- **Change:** a closed list `FORM_SECTION_TITLES` (`partyname.rs:869`), taken from the residual and the 2008/2014 form labels. `without_section_titles` (`:908`) blanks those phrases out before `names_something` in `pointer_names` (`:859`).
- **Effect:** `See section VI.3 (Additional Information)`, `See Section VI: Complementary Information`, `See Section V1.3 Additional information` and `See section V (Award of Contract)` now read `Placeholder`. NEB and Royal Courts are still kept, and so is a real body named beside a title.
- **Test:** `a_form_section_title_after_a_pointer_is_no_name` (`:2518`).

**Item 3 — politeness before the stem**
- **Change:** `POINTER_LEAD_INS` = `please`, `kindly` (`:204`), read past only as the first word, after an optional lot designator, and only directly before an anchored pointer stem (`:587`).
- **Test:** `politeness_before_a_pointer_stem_is_still_the_pointer` (`:2560`). Its keep cases include `Siemens – see section VI.3`, `Acme Ltd – please see section VI.3`, `Please Hold Ltd` and `Pleasance Theatre Trust`.
- **Cost:** `Please see section VI.4.3 Translink` (1 mention) becomes `Placeholder`. That is the same as `See section VI.4.3 Translink` today, because the keep rule needs a separator.

**Item 4 — withheld and not-applicable phrasing**
- **Change:**
  - Four withheld sentences are added as `Placeholder` whole values (`:266`).
  - Three "This is not applicable in/to the UK" spellings are added as `Blank` whole values (`:368`).
  - The `… erfolgt (hier) keine Angabe` family is a tail rule (`NO_INFORMATION_TAILS` `:379`, `withheld_by_reference` `:730`). Every word before the tail must be a legal-reference word or contain a digit, so `Stadtwerke Kiel – erfolgt keine Angabe` and `Müller GmbH (erfolgt hier keine Angabe)` stay names. These are not exact entries, so they are read before the wet run.
  - `mentions_placeholder` also names the tail rule (`:721`).
- **Test:** `withheld_and_not_applicable_sentences_have_their_class` (`:2599`). I also extended `every_entry_is_folded_and_every_stem_padded` to the new lists.

**The walk's net:** every new drop contains ` see section`, ` withheld`, ` keine angabe` or ` not applicable`, or is a whole value. Each test asserts that `mentions_placeholder` catches it.

**Residual probe** (all classes, the `non_exact` and `exempted` lists of plans 2273 and 2266):
- **Kept → dropped:** only 2 names moved from `AwardSummary` to `Placeholder`, both junk. All other moves go from name to Placeholder or Blank, and every one is a please-pointer, a withheld sentence, `erfolgt keine Angabe` or "not applicable in the UK".
- **Name → AwardSummary:** 4 junk names (about 9 mentions) moved, for example `Please see Section II.B: Object of the contract…`. `names_something` counts a bare `II` as a name. The fold keeps them as it does today; they are now listed as exempted instead of re-queued.

**Item 5 — `Withheld Section94 Supplier`, PPON `GBPPONPBXY3232WNHZ`**
- **What the code does:** I parsed an FTS release through `crate::fts::parse` with this party, named and carrying `GB-PPON-PBXY-3232-WNHZ`. The decider **drops** it as `Placeholder` and counts it in `placeholder_identified`, because the decision gives Placeholder no identifier guard. So I did not pin a "kept deliberately" test.
- **A path that keeps it:** if the FTS `parties[]` entry has no `name`, the section has no name to classify. It mints a mention with an empty name and the gated PPON, which binds by PPON to org 30914328, and the fold keeps it. This could explain the 9 surviving mentions.
- **Other explanations:** a real-named party carrying the Section94 PPON, or mention rows not re-seen by the wet run (the "planned-but-unseen" 590).
- **To tell which:** a bounded indexed read of org 30914328's 9 mention rows (name, raw identifier, section) on `organization_mentions_org`. It needs the team lead's per-read approval under `docs/agents/prod-box-reads.md`, so I did not run it.
- **Conflict to resolve:** the issue's "keep it deliberately" contradicts decision §4 guard 3, under which the code drops it. Keeping it would be a behaviour change and needs a ruling.

findings.title: Translation echo turns the pointer keep rule's separator gap into dropping a real named party
findings.scenario: I checked this with a probe test, since removed; project.rs is back to its pre-review checksum. A party has EN "See Section VI.3 Kier Construction" and DE "Siehe Abschnitt VI.3 Kier Construction". The EN copy already reads Placeholder, because `pointer_names` (partyname.rs:850-856) returns false when a reference has no separator after it. Before unit 4 the DE copy read None, so the all-names rule kept the party. Now `translation_echoes` treats DE as an echo: same token `vi.3`, label DEU vs ENG, 5 words, no legal form found. The probe returned `decided = {ORG-4: Placeholder}`, so the winner is dropped. The same happens for "See Section VI.3 Acme plc": `company_token` lacks plc, so EN reads Placeholder. `translation_shaped` also returns true for "Acme plc/LLP/Inc/A/S/AS/OÜ/d.o.o./a.s./KG VI.3", so the legal-form guard misses the forms that `summary_shape` also misses. The rule's doc says such a name "reads as no party", but the legal-form check is the only test of that, and it has these gaps. There is one case in the current residual: "Please see section VI.4.3 Translink" (1 mention, review-body). Item 3 makes it Placeholder, and on a multilingual r208 notice item 1 then drops its translations with it, which removes the whole Translink party. The build report counts that case as a single name changing class.
findings.fix: Seed the echo only from pointers whose own tail names nothing. Expose a helper from partyname, e.g. `pointer_tail_names(raw)` = `names_something(&without_section_titles(strip_references(after_stem).0))`, without the separator requirement, and skip seeds where it is true. The 460 + 144 targets still seed: "See Section VI.2 'Additional information'." leaves only a blanked title. An alternative is to refuse an echo when the translation shares a capitalised word of two or more letters with the seed, other than the section token; a proper noun copied untranslated is a name. Add a near-miss test: EN "See Section VI.3 Kier Construction" with its DE copy, and the party is kept.

findings.title: Walk's net no longer covers every echo drop: a non-English original's org is never re-queued
findings.scenario: The r209 parser walks the primary ORIGINAL copy first (r209/parse.rs:690) and the translations after it. So the party's first name, and with it `organizations.name`, is in the original language. Take a FR- or DE-original r208 award whose winner is FR "Voir point VI.2) Autres informations." or DE "siehe Abschnitt VI.2 „Sonstige Informationen“.", with TED's EN translation "See Section VI.2 'Additional information'.". The probe showed the fold drops it (`ORG-3: Placeholder`), but `mentions_placeholder` returns false for both head names. `refold-placeholder-names` reads only the head name (`orgs_named_window`, canonical.rs ~18190), so it never re-queues these orgs. Their mentions stay until some unrelated refold touches the notice. The doc claim in `translation_echoes` ("The walk's net sees the English pointer..., which the translations ride on") is false for these. The build report's "the 460 residual orgs all have English head names" does not show otherwise: the residual is the net's own hit list, so only English heads can appear in it. How many non-English-head orgs exist is unmeasured. This is the first drop rule where the head name can stay unclassified while the party drops; before it, the all-names rule meant the head name was always classified, so the net caught it.
findings.fix: Widen the walk's net to names that carry a form section token. Either add `|| !form_section_tokens(name).is_empty()` to `mentions_placeholder`, or give the walk's `net()` its own arm. The walk already re-queues every hit that is not an AwardSummary and lets the fold decide, so the extra cost is refolds. If the net is not widened, size the non-English-head population with a bounded read before the wet run, correct the doc comment, and record the gap in the issue and docs/operations.md.

findings.title: Item 1: a translation that names a body after the shared number is swept, and no keep test covers it
findings.scenario: A party has EN "See section VI.4.3 Translink" and DE "Siehe Abschnitt VI.4.3 Translink". The EN is already Placeholder today: the keep rule needs a separator, the same as the residual's 'Please see section VI.4.3 Translink' (review-body, 3 mentions), which item 3 now makes Placeholder. The DE reads None, carries vi.4.3, is labelled DE (not EN), has 4 words and no legal form, so translation_echoes sweeps it. The whole party drops. Before unit 4 the DE name kept it. 'See Section VI.3 Kier Construction' + 'Siehe Abschnitt VI.3 Kier Construction' fails the same way. None of the eight keep-test near misses has a body name with no legal form after the number, so the suite cannot see this loss. Items 1 and 3 together turn the accepted single-language cost into a real-party drop in multilingual notices.
findings.fix: Seed the echo only from bare pointers: a Placeholder that names nothing once the section reference is stripped and the form-section titles are blanked, i.e. `!names_something(&without_section_titles(strip_references(after_stem(..)).0))`, exposed from partyname as a pub helper. 'See Section VI.2 'Additional information'.' and 'See section VI.3 (Additional Information)' still seed; 'See section VI.4.3 Translink' does not. Add a keep case to a_name_beside_a_translated_pointer_that_reads_as_a_party_keeps_it: (EN 'See section VI.4.3 Translink', DE 'Siehe Abschnitt VI.4.3 Translink').

findings.title: Item 1: the AwardSummary near miss (ORG-8) is also protected by its legal form, so the AwardSummary exclusion is never tested

The review body's party drops, and nothing fails.
findings.fix: Change ORG-8's translation, or add a case, so it reads AwardSummary with no legal form and 12 words or fewer, e.g. (Some("DE"), "siehe oben: Vergabekammer Südbayern (VI.3)"). Assert the premise `not_a_name(..) == Some(AwardSummary)` and `translation_shaped(..)` so it stays a real near miss.

findings.title: Item 1: the 24-language drop test uses 7 reconstructed strings, so it cannot show that notice 12516947 drops
findings.scenario: The PL, SK, SL, GA, BG, RO and HR entries in TED_VI2_POINTER were written from TED labels. The prod read shows PL as 'Zob. sekcja VI. ...'. The party drops only if EVERY name is classified. If one real copy writes the number differently ('VI. 2', 'VI 2', a Cyrillic or Greek homoglyph for I, or a localised section word that splits the token), form_section_tokens returns [] for it. findings.title: Item 1: the seed-side conditions are unpinned (an unlabelled seed, a non-Placeholder seed), and ORG-6 does not isolate what its comment claims
findings.scenario: Every seed in the tests is a labelled Placeholder. Mutate the seed filter at 4636 to `class.is_some_and(|c| c != AwardSummary)` and all tests pass. Then FR 'Non attribué (voir VI.3)' (VoidLot) + NL 'Stad Gent (VI.3)' (None, 3 words, no form) sweeps the NL name. findings.title: Item 4 tail rule: no test pins the end anchor, 'gemass' misses German 'gemäß', and a name with a digit before the tail reads as a placeholder
findings.scenario: (a) Mutate `padded.strip_suffix(tail)` to take the text before the first `find(tail)` and every test passes. 'Erfolgt keine Angabe – Auftragnehmer: Stadtwerke Kiel' would then read Placeholder, because an empty head is vacuously all reference words. No keep case has text after the phrase. (b) fold_latin maps ß to s, so 'Gemäß' folds to 'gemas'; the residual's own fold shows 'keine angabe gemas 62 abs 3 bvergg 2018'. The entry 'gemass' only matches the Swiss spelling. 'Gemäß § 39 Abs. 6 VgV erfolgt keine Angabe' stays a name, and every_entry_is_folded cannot catch this because 'gemass' folds to itself. (c) The 'any word with a digit' arm has no near-miss test: '3M – erfolgt keine Angabe' reads Placeholder. (d) The whole-value keep cases 'Information Withheld Ltd' and 'Due Diligence Partners Ltd' read None before and after the change, so they pin nothing.
findings.fix: Add 'gemas' to REFERENCE_HEAD_WORDS and a positive case 'Gemäß § 39 Abs. 6 VgV erfolgt keine Angabe'. Add a keep case with text after the tail (e.g. 'Erfolgt keine Angabe – Auftragnehmer: Stadtwerke Kiel'). Either require a digit-bearing head word to also be at least two characters or a §-style number, or pin '3M – erfolgt keine Angabe' as an accepted cost.

findings.title: `gemass` in REFERENCE_HEAD_WORDS never matches the fold of `gemäß`, so `Gemäß … erfolgt keine Angabe` stays a name
findings.scenario: `fold` = buyer_name_fold(match_norm(..)). fold_latin maps 'ß' to a single 's' (store canonical.rs `'ß' => 's'`), so `gemäß` folds to `gemas`, never `gemass`. Probe run with the gate flags: not_a_name("Gemäß § 39 Abs. 6 VgV erfolgt keine Angabe") = None, while "gem. § 39 …" and the ASCII "gemass § 39 …" both give Some(Placeholder). The list's own test (`fold(word) == word`) passes because `gemass` is ASCII, so it cannot catch this. The miss errs toward keeping the party, and none of the residual's 'erfolgt' names uses `gemäß`, so it is a dead entry, not a loss. The same probe shows an Austrian `… BVergG 2018 erfolgt keine Angabe` also stays a name (`bvergg` is not in the list).
findings.fix: Add `gemas` (the fold of gemäß) beside `gemass`, and add a `Gemäß § 39 Abs. 6 VgV erfolgt keine Angabe` case to `withheld_and_not_applicable_sentences_have_their_class`. Optionally add `bvergg` if Austrian phrasing is wanted.

findings.title: withheld_by_reference allocates a padded String for almost every party name in the fold; its clause in mentions_placeholder can never decide anything
findings.scenario: not_a_name_in now evaluates `PLACEHOLDER_WHOLE.contains(&whole) || withheld_by_reference(whole)` for every name that reaches the whole-value stage, which is nearly every real name. drop_decision calls not_a_name once per party name per notice, so every folded notice pays one extra `format!(" {whole}")` heap allocation per real party name, on top of the fold and `padded` the function already builds. In mentions_placeholder (the walk's predicate over org head names) the added `|| withheld_by_reference(whole)` only runs after the ` keine angabe` stem check, which `padded.contains` already returns true for on any name the tail rule could match (the comment admits this). The clause can never change the result, but it costs one allocation for every name the net does not catch.
findings.fix: Match without padding, e.g. `NO_INFORMATION_TAILS.iter().find_map(|t| whole.strip_suffix(&t[1..])).filter(|h| h.is_empty() || h.ends_with(' '))`, then run the head-word test on `h`. Or return early unless `whole.ends_with("angabe") || whole.ends_with("angaben")`. Drop the clause from mentions_placeholder and keep only the comment, or leave the clause and use the allocation-free form.

findings.title: translation_echoes' doc says the walk's net sees the English pointer; it only sees the org's head name, and docs/operations.md does not mention the echo
findings.scenario: refold-placeholder-names applies mentions_placeholder to the org's stored head name: the first name in parse order, which is the ORIGINAL form copy (r209/parse.rs walks the LG_ORIG original first, translations after). Take a TED r208 award whose original is DE and whose winner is the VI.2 pointer. The head name is `siehe Abschnitt VI.2 „Sonstige Informationen“.`, mentions_placeholder is false, and the walk never re-queues the party. The fold would drop it only when something else touches the notice. The build agent's '460 residual orgs all have English head names' cannot rule this out: the plan lists only net hits, so parties with non-English heads never appear in it. docs/operations.md (in scope for this unit) still describes the fold's keeps and the walk's net without the translation echo or this gap, so the unit-4 wet run's floor and residual could be misread.
findings.fix: Reword the doc: the net sees the English pointer only when the English copy is the original, and a party whose original copy is a translation drains through touched-notice folds. Add a short paragraph to the issue-511 section of docs/operations.md: the echo rule (same section number, another labelled language, translation-shaped), and that the walk's net cannot see a pointer party whose head name is a non-English copy.

findings.title: Parallel `labels` map duplicates the tally's per-owner bookkeeping in drop_decision
findings.scenario: drop_decision runs once per folded notice. The change adds a second HashMap<&str, Vec<Option<&str>>>: one more hash lookup per party name and one more Vec allocation per party, kept 'index for index' with `tally`, and then `&labels[owner]` (a panicking index) to rejoin the two. That is not a storm, but it doubles the decider's per-party allocations for a label that is only read when a party holds a Placeholder that carries a section number, and the two parallel vectors must stay the same length by convention.
findings.fix: Carry the label in the tally entry, `Vec<(&str, Option<NotAName>, Option<&str>)>`, or a small struct, and have translation_echoes take that slice. That removes the second map, the double lookup and the `labels[owner]` index.

fix:
The four code findings were real and are now fixed with tests. Findings 6 and 7 (item 5) were real too, but they need a decision from you rather than a code change, so I only recorded them in the issue file. The focused 511 tests pass on the final source: EXIT=0 on two runs, 76 tests, none failed. Nothing is committed.

| # | Real? | What I did |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Yes | Fixed (seed rule below), with keep tests |
| 2 | Yes | Fixed (net widened below), with tests |
| 3 | Yes | Fixed together with finding 1 |
| 4 | Yes | Added a keep case only the class guard protects |
| 5 | Yes | No code fix possible here; added a stop check to the canary instead |
| 6 + 7 | Yes | No code change; conflict written into the issue file |

**1 and 3 — a body named after the section number got dropped.** By the code, EN `See Section VI.3 Kier Construction` and `Please see section VI.4.3 Translink` both read as `Placeholder`, and their DE copies read as names. So the translation rule swept the DE copy and dropped a real party.
- **Fix:** a new public function in `partyname.rs`, `names_after_stem(name)`, asks whether the text after the stem names something, without requiring a separator. In `project.rs`, the translation rule now starts only from placeholders where that answer is no.
- **Targets still drop:** `See Section VI.2 'Additional information'.` and `See section VI.3 (Additional Information)` still start the sweep, so the 460 + 144 mentions are unaffected.
- **Side effect:** a capitalised ordinary noun after the number also stops the sweep (`Please see section VI.3 for list of awarded Suppliers`). That errs toward keeping a name.
- **Legal forms:** I moved the stem-finding code into a helper (`placeholder_hit`) so both readers share it. I also added `plc`, `LLP`, `Inc`, `LLC`, `KG`, `AS`, `A/S`, `OÜ`, `d.o.o.` and `a.s.` to the legal-form check.

**2 — the drain job can't see non-English originals.** Confirmed by reading the code: the TED parser (`r209/parse.rs`) walks the original-language copy first, and the drain job (`refold-placeholder-names`) reads only `organizations.name`. A FR-original party therefore has the French text as its head name, which the old filter missed. That filter, `mentions_placeholder`, picks which organisations the job re-queues. It now also catches any name of 12 words or fewer, with a section number like `VI.2` and no legal form. That is exactly what the translation rule can sweep. The cost: short real names that cite a section, such as a `Referat II.3`-style name, get refolded and will show in the next dry run's `name` count.

**4 — the AwardSummary guard was never tested on its own.** Added ORG-10, a DE copy `siehe oben: Vergabekammer Südbayern (VI.3)`. The test asserts it is an `AwardSummary` and has the translated shape, so nothing but its class protects it.

**Mutation check for 1, 3 and 4.** With both the new seed filter and the class guard removed, the keep test fails with `{"ORG-10": Placeholder, "ORG-11": Placeholder, "ORG-12": Placeholder}` (EXIT=101). I then restored `project.rs` and checked its sha256 against the backup.

**5 — seven of the 24 translations in the test are made up.** I can't get the real strings without a prod read, which needs your go-ahead, so I didn't do one. The test comment now says the PL, SK, SL, GA, BG, RO and HR strings are reconstructions. The canary in the issue file and `docs/operations.md` now refolds 12516947 and 19530163. A key lookup must find no `organization_mentions` row for ORG-2 or ORG-10, and the run stops if either survives.

**6 and 7 — item 5 says keep, everything else says drop.** The issue asks to keep `Withheld Section94 Supplier`. That contradicts:
- decision §4 guard 3;
